headline: Figma Make Skills Change Everything
subheadline: Figma's May release introduces Make Skills — reusable markdown prompts for prototyping consistency. Plus, MCP roundtrip workflows are maturing fast, and design systems are going agentic.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Figma Release Notes 2026: May Edition
sections.description: The big one this month: Make Skills — markdown-based reusable prompts that enforce your team's conventions when generating prototypes. For your white-label sport apps design system, this could be massive. Also covers Make voice-to-text, FigJam MCP server improvements, and new AI image tools. Worth a full watch.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma AI in 2026: Everything it can do — and what it still can't
sections.description: An honest, comprehensive breakdown of where Figma AI actually stands right now — Dev Mode, Code Connect, MCP server, and Make. The framing that Figma is evolving from design tool to AI-assisted product design platform mirrors exactly the shift you're navigating. Good for calibrating what to bet on vs. what's still half-baked.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Make Skills: Markdown as design system governance
sections.description: Figma's Make Skills let you write markdown files that encode your team's design conventions, so AI-generated prototypes follow your rules out of the box. Think of it as design system documentation that's actually executable. For your white-label system, this could replace hours of QA-ing AI output — your tokens and component rules become the prompt itself.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: The Future of Enterprise Design Systems: Agentic AI in 2026
sections.description: Supernova's take on design systems going agentic — automating governance, scaling with AI, and future-proofing product workflows. Directly relevant to what you're building with Figma MCP + Claude. The practical roadmap framing makes this more useful than most trend pieces.

sections.label: Listen
sections.title: How AI Agents Will Transform in 2026 (a16z Big Ideas)
sections.description: a16z unpacks three shifts: AI moving from chat to action, agent-native product design, and what comes next. Great stroller listen. You're already vibe-coding — this gives you the strategic vocabulary for where agent-driven product building is heading and how product leaders should think about it.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: AI Design Systems Conference 2026 recordings now available
sections.description: 15+ hours of recordings from the sold-out March conference. Sessions on vibe coding, agentic design systems, MCP integrations, and shipping production-ready code from design. Cherry-pick the MCP and agentic sessions — they'll be directly applicable to your current build.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If your design system conventions become executable prompts, what's the new role of a design system lead?
sections.description: Make Skills turns your documentation into AI instructions. Supernova and others are making governance automated. If the system enforces itself, the lead's value shifts from consistency policing to strategic decisions: what conventions exist in the first place, and why. That's product leadership territory — which is exactly where you're heading.
